rules.text:
Eligibility

Note: Players should be registered members of the church with their names in parishonnet. Registration would require FID and validation will be purely based on parishonet data. Captains will be given the list of players by Aug 28th and they can challenge the data till Sep 1st. No change to the data will be done after that even if it is known that a player belongs to a different ward.


No replacement will be allowed outside of the registered team

How about a new parishioner joining during the event or moving wards during the event? 


Eligibility for Independent Ward Participation

Although the teams are organized into groups consisting of multiple wards, each individual ward may participate independently in any of the five game categories if that ward has enough players to form a complete team for that particular game.

  • Consent of Group Captains

A ward may form a separate team only when all captains representing the wards within that group agree to allow the ward to participate independently. 

  • Game-by-Game Participation

Independent participation will be considered separately for each game. A ward may:

  • Participate as part of its original group team in one game; and

  • Participate as an independent ward team in another game,

provided the required team size is met and the relevant group captains have agreed. Approval is required on a game-by-game basis, and the independent ward team must comply with all rules and requirements applicable to other teams.

Ans: This will not be entertained. They will stay with the ward if they have moved after Sep 1, 2026

Although the teams are organized into groups consisting of multiple wards, each individual ward may participate independently in any of the five game categories if that ward has enough players to form a complete team for that particular game.

Consent of Group Captains
A ward may form a separate team only when all captains representing the wards within that group agree to allow the ward to participate independently.
Game-by-Game Participation
Independent participation will be considered separately for each game. A ward may:

Participate as part of its original group team in one game; and
Participate as an independent ward team in another game, provided the required team size is met and the relevant group captains, from original grouping, have agreed. Approval is required on a game-by-game basis, and the independent ward team must comply with all rules and requirements applicable to other teams.

  • St Euphrasia/St Paul

• There will be a total of 5 games in a match between two teams

    • 2 OD (Open Doubles)

    • 2 XD (Mixed Doubles)

    • 1 WD (Female Doubles)

  • Leagues matches would be 21 points, whichever team reaches 21 will win. If a game is at 20-20, then the team that gains a 2-point difference will win, or the team that reaches 25(max point will win) whichever happens first (League Matches)

  • 1 Point will be awarded for each win. The team who gains more points will be the winner of the match

  • Max of 10 players can form a team(Recommended). Min of 6 players are required (4 men and 2 women). Teams can register with max of 12 players.

  • A player can play max of 2 games in different categories. 

  • Courts can be switched after 15 points (League Matches)

  • Toss would decide the court/serve. The team that wins the toss can decide to pick between court or serve. 

  • Teams will be ordered based on points and the top two teams will play finals. Third and Fourth place will be decided based on the league match result. If two teams share the same point then the team which had won in the league match will be ranked on top.If there is a situation where we cannot decide based on the league match results then a draw will decide the winner.

  • Finals will be best of 3 and will be played for 21 points. If a game is at 20-20, then the team that gains a 2-point difference will win, or the team that reaches 25(max point will win) whichever happens first

  • If the birdie touches any of the internal structures then it would be declared a foul and the point will be awarded to the opponent

  • Players need to bring rackets and wear non marking shoes

  • Team captain has to provide the players for a game before the start of the game.

  • Referee decision is final

Team Structure

 

  • There will be 5 games played between two wards/group. Each ward will have 3 player group and will play 3 Open , 1 Mixed (one women player is mandatory) and a Women. The ward/group which wins 3 of their games between wards will be declared winner for that particular game between two wards/group and will get a point awarded. 
  • There will be multiple such matches against different wards/groups based on schedule.
  • Finals will be played between the ward/group with maximum points. If there is a tie the points accumulated during the league matches will be considered.
  • A player can play 2 distinct categories at the max for a given match between two wards


Playing Rules


A. General game rules and objectives:


1. 36 cards from standard 52-deck cards are used for playing this game. There are nine

cards from each suit: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs and Spades.

2. Cards used with their ranks/values: J=3, 9=2, A & 10 = 1 (A > 10), K, Q, 8, 7 & 6 = 0 (K > Q

> 8 > 7 > 6) add to a total of 28 points with 4 suits.

3. The objective of the game is to obtain a higher score of points than the opposing team

at the end of a session or regulation play.

4. Two partnerships of three players each are needed to play 28. Partners take alternate

seats.

5. The game consists of dealing, bidding (often called auction) and play after which the

hand is scored. The bid ends with a contract, which is a declaration of one partnership

that its side will take at least the declared number of points with a specified suit as

trumps.

6. A minimum bid of 16 in suits is mandatory for the lead player, seated to the immediate

right of the dealer. This will be followed by higher bids by other players in a

counterclockwise direction up to a maximum bid of 28 in any of the four suits.

7. Win tricks to collect card points. The bidding team must meet or exceed their bid. The

opponents try to stop them.

8. The following point scoring system will be maintained for all individual deals, and points

will be recorded in score sheets. Cumulative scores will be determined at the end of

each session or regulation play.

9. A fulfilled bid or contract of 16-19 gets 1 score point, 20 to 23 scores 2, 24-27 scores 3,

28 scores 4, ‘Thani’ or ‘Adi’ scores 5.

10. In the event a bid/contract is defeated, the team which defeats the bid/contract gets

the following points: 16-19 gets 2 score point, 20 to 23 scores 3, 24-27 scores 4, 28

scores 5, ‘Thani’ or ‘Adi’ scores 6.

11. ക ോട്ട്:

a. Applicable to the contracts 16 through 19.

b. Needs to be called by the bidding team (only the lead player) when at least 2

rounds of cards are yet to play and in procession of all the folded tricks that

were already played.

c. d. e. Once the ക ോട്ട് is locked, the bidding team has to catch all the tricks.

Non-bidding team (only the player in turn) can ask the ക ോട്ട് at any time

ക ോട്ട് call should only be answered by the player who holds the trick at

that time

f. A fulfilled ക ോട്ട് will get 2 points for the bidding team. If fails, the opponent gets

3 points.

g. Only the lead player at any given moment can call/accept ക ോട്ട്. Only the player in

turn of the opposite team can ask for ക ോട്ട്.. Out of turn asking/calling or

accepting the ‘ക ോട്ട്.’ will result points (point 11.f) to the other team.

h. Both teams must ensure that all folded tricks are with the bidding team beforecalling or asking a ക ോട്ട്. Failure to fulfill this rule will be treated as a loss, and

points will be awarded in accordance with Point 11.f.

12. മറു ക ോട്ട്:

a. Applicable to the contracts 16 through 19.

b. The bidding team can ask at any round of the play. The opposite team has to call മറു

ക ോട്ട് before the last lead.

c. A fulfilled മറു ക ോട്ട് ട്ട് will get 3 points for the team opposite to the bidding

team. If it fails, the bidding team gets 2 points.

d. Only the lead player at any given moment can call/accept മറു ക ോട്ട്


B. Dealing of cards:


13. The deal, dealer and game are played/moved counterclockwise, the dealer rotating by game.

14. Cards are to be dealt first by the player determined by the draw. The next deal is to be

performed by the player sitting immediately to the right of the dealer and so on.

15. The dealer will shuffle the cards thoroughly using both hands. Table flopping (as is done

in the game of Rummy) is not permitted.

16. The cards are then offered to the player seated immediately to the left for “cutting”, an

action of restacking performed by one hand in a single motion. Multiple restacking is not

allowed

17. Cards will be dealt three at a time, face down in a counterclockwise direction in two (2)

rounds, thus each player gets 6 cards in total.

18. Re-Deal of Hands: The following infractions when occur will cause the hand to be re-

dealt by the same dealer who caused the constraints:

a. If any card is exposed during the process of the deal.

b. If any player gets more than or less than 6 cards.

c. If a player is dealt with all 6 cards in the same suit.

d. If a player is dealt with all 4 Jacks.

e. If after the bid and during the play it is discovered that the defending team is

collectively void in trumps.

f. Out-of-turn shuffle will result in reshuffle if detected before the start of the

game, i.e., before the first card is played by the leading player.


C. Bidding (Auction):


19. A minimum bid of 16 is compulsory for player to the immediate right of the dealer,

entering in the Call Count. The bidder tables the trump face down on the table, visible to

all players.

20. The opposite team member sitting immediate right to the opening player gets a chance

for a higher bid. A 'pass' by this opposite team player means the opposite team’s second

player gets a chance to raise the bid. If he/she passes, the opposite team’s third player

(dealer) gets a chance to make a higher bid. If any of the players from opposite team

raises the bid and puts their trump face down on the table, the opening player’s

teammate (second followed by third) gets a chance to raise the bid. If the opposite team

does not raise the bid, the opening team’s partner(s) can raise the bid to the next higher

level. i.e. if the opening player calls 16, and the opposite team does not raise the bid,

the opening team’s partner(s) can call 20 or higher to make his/her own trump. Dealing

and the turn occur in an anticlockwise direction.

21. Bidding is permitted only at one’s turn. Out of turn ‘bidding’ or out of turn discarding

card’ can result in a one-time warning and for subsequent violations a penalty of one (1)

point is awarded to the opposing team for each such violation. The issue has to be

raised by the opposing team when the violation occurs.

 

D. Play of the Hand:

 

22. Play for the 1st trick is initiated by the player to the right of the dealer.

23. The lead player cannot start with a card he/ she has made the final bid upon (Trump),

until it is opened by a player for trumping a void suit played or he/she holds no other

suit. The bidder can discard the trump card without being opened if he doesn’t have the

same suite.

24. Playing with all trumps in one hand or within the same team nullifies the game.

25. Out of turn leading or play is not allowed. Any infraction in this regard whether

intentional or not, can result in a “warning” for the first violation, and after that in a

penalty of one (1) point if objected to by the opposing team.

26. The other players must follow suit. You can either trump or discard another card, if you

are void in the suit led. You click on the face-down trump card to open it, to trump the

suit.

27. Having called for the trump to be exposed, you must play a trump to this trick if you

have one; if you have no trump, you may discard any card.

28. It’s not necessary to use the face-down trump at first time for the bidder.

29. The highest card in the suit wins the trick, unless it is trumped. The highest trump wins

the trick.

30. When all six tricks have been played, each side counts the card points in the tricks they

have won. The bidding team needs at least as many card points as the bid to win;

otherwise, they lose.

31. The cumulative scores of the two teams are recorded on a piece of paper. The number

of game points scored depends on the bid, not on the exact number of points taken in

tricks.

32. To make a trump, the bidder must have at least one card of that suit. If he/she only has

one trump and he/she has put it face down as the trump, and if any of the 5 other

players plays the trump, he/she cannot open the trump and play that card.


E. Miscellaneous:


33 For ‘Thani’ or ‘Adi’ call/bid

a. All 6 players need to play (not just the defending team and the ‘Thani’ bidder).

b. Minimum 2 Adi is a must (Top 2 cards, J and 9 of same suits) to make Thani bid.

c. Starting Suit cards should be over by the time Thani bidder runs out of that suit

(Ex: Thani bidder has Spade J 9 A, Hearts J 9, Clubs J. Once Thani bidder plays all

those 3 Spades, all the 9 spades should be played. Let us say another player

holds 4 Spades, by the time Thani bidder plays Spade A, that player still will have

one Spade left in which case Thani bid will be considered defeated).

d. ‘Sure Thani’ is not allowed – Ex: Thani bidder has Hearts J, 9, A, 10, K and Spade

J (there is no way opponent has a chance here, hence ‘Sure Thani’).

e. 'Sure Thani' hand can be bidden and played with a trump as long as the play/

cards do not come under 'Re-Deal of Hands' mentioned in section B-18.

34 Cardinal Rule: Each player must follow through with the same suit 'in play', if player holds

cards in the same suit. Only if you have no cards of that suit, you can play a trump, or

discard any card.

a. Discarding of Jacks is allowed (Jacks treated as any other cards when it comes to

discarding).

b. If any player violates the cardinal rules, their team is penalized by awarding the

'game' and three (3) additional points to the opposing team. Awarding the game

in the following order: If the team that violated the rule has 'sealed' the bid,

they have lost the game. If the other team has sealed the bid, then they have

won that game.

35 If a player tables two or more cards at one’s turn, it is declaration of claim of all

remaining tricks. If the opposing team challenges this claim, they have an option to36 simulate the play and disprove the claim by using any permutation or combination. If

that possibility is established, all those remaining tricks will be claimed en bloc by the

challenging team. This however does not affect the status of tricks already won prior to

the challenge.

A card exposed and placed on table cannot be retired and substituted with another

card from the same suite unless extenuating circumstances. An Extenuating

circumstance is the accidental slip from the hand of a player before a play is

commenced or rather a new lead in play is commenced.

37 No tricks or codes are allowed. This includes body language, coughing or making sounds,

unnecessary comments, etc. If any team is found to be in violation, they may be

disqualified or the opposing team awarded three (3) points for that game.

38 No talking or gestures are allowed during the game. All are requested to maintain

decorum and sportsmanship during the entire duration of the tournament.

39 40 41 Calling the suites in one language is strongly recommended.

If any player is passing the call, please call ‘Pass’

Trump card should be kept parallel to the body on the table.

42 Players within the team can switch any number of times before the shuffle.

Switching seats between opposite teams is allowed only one time after the half

way of the game.

43 At no time, a team together should throw the cards together on the table

alleging a violation, when the game is in progress. If any player alleges any

violation, every player will hold onto his/her cards until a resolution is made.

44 In case of any dispute, the decision of the Match referee shall be final and

binding. The match referee and their panel will be announced prior to the

commencement of the tournament.

45 Only a few specific issues are mentioned here, all the general rules are applied to the game of

28 (support) will be followed in this tournament.

46 The Organizing committee has the right to add or amend the existing rules if

necessary

47 There is no external referee or umpire for any match. The progress of the match is to be

monitored and recorded by the players themselves.

48 Number of Shuffles – League – 12, Knock out/Semi – 12, Final – 12

49 Tie-Breaker:

a. This is needed from the knock-out stage only. In the preliminary league round, if the

total cumulative score for both the teams is the same, each team will get one (1)

match point.

b. Knock-Out round tie-breaker will be applied as follows: After the stipulated number

of games, if the total cumulative points for the both the teams are the same, the

game will be continuing for 2 more deals in the same order. If the score is still tied,

there will be just one more game played after tossing to find the dealer of that

game. The toss can be employed by the two captains pulling one card each from the

stack of cards.
